title: YouTube yapay zeka destekli özel akışlar ve yeni özelliklerini duyurdu
summary: YouTube, Made on YouTube etkinliğinde yapay zeka destekli özel akışlar, Ask YouTube ve YouTube Music için yeni sohbet tabanlı araçları tanıttı.
body:
YouTube, yıllık Made on YouTube etkinliğinde platformun kullanıcılar ve içerik üreticileri için yenilenen yüzünü paylaştı. Yapılan duyurulara göre, Google’ın video platformu yapay zeka teknolojilerini arayüze ve müzik uygulamasına entegre eden yeni araçlar sunmaya hazırlanıyor.

## Özel akışlar ve yapay zeka entegrasyonu
TechCrunch'ın aktardığına göre, kullanıcılar kendi algoritmalarını oluşturmalarına imkan tanıyan yeni **özel akışlar** (custom feeds) özelliğine kavuşuyor. İstediğiniz bir konuyu ya da ruh halini metin kutusuna yazarak Google’ın Gemini AI modelinin bu doğrultuda yeni bir sekme oluşturmasını sağlayabilirsiniz. YouTube'un açıklamasına göre bu özellik, kullanıcıların platformdaki yüz milyarlarca video arasından istedikleri içeriklere daha kolay ulaşmasını hedefliyor. Özelliğin web ve mobil platformlarda önümüzdeki ay itibarıyla kullanıma sunulması planlanıyor.

## YouTube Music ve sohbet özellikleri
Etkinlikte ayrıca YouTube Music uygulaması için de yeni yapay zeka yetenekleri duyuruldu. Ask Music adlı yeni sohbet tabanlı araç, arama çubuğunun yerine geçerek kullanıcıların günlük dille şarkı, çalma listesi veya sanatçı aramasına olanak tanıyor. Platform ayrıca, podcast keşfini kolaylaştırmak için Your Podcast Lineup adlı yeni bir yapay zeka rehberi sunuyor. Öte yandan Ars Technica'nın haberine göre, platforma gelecek diğer yenilikler arasında şu maddeler yer alıyor:

- Yorumlarda GIF paylaşımı desteği
- Doğrudan mesajlaşma özelliğine grup sohbeti eklenmesi
- Ürün inceleme videolarında ve aramalarda daha aktif rol alan Ask YouTube asistanı

**Neden önemli?** Bu yenilikler, YouTube'un kullanıcı deneyimini daha kişiselleştirilmiş ve etkileşimli hale getirmek için yapay zeka araçlarını platform genelinde daha belirgin bir konuma taşıdığını gösteriyor.

source_texts.title: YouTube promises custom feeds and a lot more AI later this year
source_texts.summary: YouTube's next year could change the content you see with a big focus on AI and livestreams.
source_texts.text:
The annual Made on YouTube event has just wrapped up, offering an early look at the features you can expect to come to Google’s dominant online streaming platform in the coming months. Yes, there’s plenty of AI for both viewers and creators, but there’s also a handful of non-AI updates mixed in there, too.
The design of YouTube’s homepage feed comes under fire often, but the platform is preparing to give you more options. With Custom Feeds, you’ll be able to add new tabs to the YouTube interface with content of your choice. To create a feed, just type a description and let YouTube populate the page. You can refine your description and rate video suggestions to tune the Custom Feed. Google says you’ll be able to save “multiple” feeds without specifying the exact number. This feature will roll out soon in the US for web, mobile, and TV users.
Interacting on YouTube will also change later this year. The platform will finally add the option to post GIFs in comments, which has apparently been a common request for some time. The comment box will let you search for popular animated thumbnails and post them on both regular videos and YouTube Shorts. The YouTube direct messaging feature is also adding support for group chat, but it’s only going to be available in the US, UK, Singapore, Brazil, and some European countries to start.
YouTube is probably going to nudge you to chat with a robot more often, too. The AI-powered Ask YouTube feature is not new, but it’s getting several new features that will make it more prominent across the platform. The AI will take on a conversational role in product review videos, allowing you to type or use voice commands to get more information about a product. In search, Ask YouTube may offer organized video recommendations and product comparison tables, too.
The music version of this AI is also expanding. Ask Music is getting more prominent placement in the YouTube Music app, right at the top where search used to be (it recently moved to a tab at the bottom). Ask Music can create or edit playlists and tell you about an artist. It will also surface suggestions throughout the app, like when you’re creating a mix.

source_texts.title: YouTube Music gets more conversational with new AI features
source_texts.summary: Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists.
source_texts.text:
YouTube is adding new AI-powered features to YouTube Music that aim to make it easier for listeners to discover music, explore artists, and find podcasts they may otherwise miss.
Announced at this year’s Made On YouTube event, the updates include “Ask Music,” a conversational tool for music and podcasts, and “Your Podcast Lineup,” a personalized audio guide designed to help listeners discover new shows.
Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists. The feature works across YouTube Music’s catalog of more than 300 million songs, including official recordings, remixes, live performances, covers, and DJ sets. Users can use it to build custom listening queues, explore an artist’s motivations, or dig deeper into music history.
YouTube explains that, instead of manually searching, the user simply types the request as if they were asking a friend. For instance, someone could ask Ask Music to create a mix based on the tracks that inspired a particular song. Users can also ask other questions, such as who played bass on a particular song or other details about its creation.
YouTube Music is also introducing Your Podcast Lineup, a personalized AI-generated audio guide for podcast discovery.
The feature is designed for a familiar problem: There are more podcasts than most people have time to listen to. Even listeners who already have a list of favorite shows can struggle to keep up with new episodes, let alone find new ones.
Your Podcast Lineup will appear on the podcast page in the YouTube Music app. Each week, it will provide a short spoken preview of recommended shows and explain why they might appeal to the listener. It can then move directly into suggested episodes.
Spotify recently introduced an AI-powered feature that follows a similar direction. Its personal podcasts feature uses AI to generate podcast episodes based on their interests and prompts.
The new features are part of YouTube’s broader push to use AI throughout its services. Last year, YouTube Music experimented with AI-powered music hosts that provide stories, fan trivia, and commentary related to what users are listening to.
Both updates are coming soon to YouTube Music and YouTube Premium subscribers worldwide.

source_texts.title: YouTube will let you build your own algorithm with AI
source_texts.summary: YouTube’s new custom feeds let users describe the videos they want to see in their own words, then use Gemini to build a personalized feed around the request.
source_texts.text:
YouTube says it’s going to let you build your own algorithm — well, kind of. The company on Wednesday announced a new feature called custom feeds that allows you to describe, in your own words, the kinds of videos you’d like YouTube to recommend to you.
To create one, you type a description of what you want the feed to be about into a prompt box on YouTube, whether that’s a feed dedicated to a particular interest or one that serves some other purpose. For instance, YouTube suggests you could build a feed of video podcasts to watch during your 30-minute train commute, or you could request videos for a particular mood, like “relaxing commentary videos to unwind with.”
The prompt-based feature leverages Google’s Gemini AI model to build the feed around your request, and the resulting feed is then pinned to the top of your YouTube home page in its own tab. Because the feed’s creation is AI-powered, the request can be described in lengthy terms, as you share detailed information about how you want to curate the feed, what it should feature or exclude, what content to prioritize, and more.
The addition follows similar moves by a number of other social networks that have created tools that essentially allow users to build their own algorithms by describing what they want their feed to include and how to present that information to them.
Decentralized social network Bluesky began popularizing this idea years ago as a way to differentiate its service from rivals like X. This year, it rolled out an AI tool, Attie, that makes feed-building even easier. Other services, including Meta’s Threads, Instagram, X, and, more recently, Spotify, have also launched their own feed-building features, many of which are also AI-powered.
YouTube believes custom feeds will help users better explore the vast number of videos now hosted on its platform.
“One of the amazing things about being on YouTube is that the world is always at your fingertips,” noted Emily Moxley, VP of Product Management for Viewer AI, in a pre-brief with reporters ahead of the Made On YouTube event on Wednesday, where custom feeds were introduced to the public. “There’s over 20 billion videos in the YouTube corpus, so you’re always one search away from a treasure trove of topics.”
The new feeds, however, will not replace YouTube’s main feed, which features all your recommendations. Instead, you will now be able to easily hop right into whichever feed best suits your purposes when you open the YouTube app.
Support for creating multiple custom feeds will roll out across YouTube on web and mobile, starting next month, the company said.
